articles.title: Jhansi: Daughter-in-Law Stages Dharna with Infant, In-Laws Lock Gate Amid Murder Plot Allegations
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh): High drama unfolded late Wednesday evening in Rai Vihar Colony near Narayan Bagh when a 30-year-old woman staged a sit-in protest outside her in-laws’ house, holding her infant daughter in her lap, after allegedly being denied entry.

body.html:
Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh): High drama unfolded late Wednesday evening in Rai Vihar Colony near Narayan Bagh when a 30-year-old woman staged a sit-in protest outside her in-laws’ house, holding her infant daughter in her lap, after allegedly being denied entry.

The woman, identified as Varsha Rai, a resident of Hansari, claimed she was married to Ravi Rai on November 24, 2024. She alleged that after the birth of her daughter, her husband and in-laws began harassing her for not bearing a son and were now trying to force her out so that Ravi could remarry.

According to Varsha, shortly after her marriage, she received a call from a woman claiming to be Ravi’s first wife. She said the family later admitted to a “mistake,” and she did not pursue the matter further. However, she now alleges that her husband is having an affair with another woman and intends to marry her with the support of his parents.

Varsha stated that she had been staying at her parental home for around one and a half months. When she returned on Monday, she was allegedly not allowed inside the house. On Wednesday, she claimed her husband left the house and switched off his phone. Left with no option, she sat outside the locked gate in protest.

On the other hand, her mother-in-law, Rajkumari, denied the allegations and accused Varsha of plotting to kill her son. She claimed that her son had read a message on Varsha’s phone allegedly stating, “If you say so, we will shoot your husband.” She also alleged that Varsha frequently stayed at her parents’ house and did not reside regularly with her in-laws.

As the confrontation escalated, police reached the spot and brought both parties to the police station. Inspector Ravi Srivastava said efforts are being made to mediate between the two sides and that further action will be taken as per legal provisions.

The incident remained the subject of intense discussion in the locality as accusations and counter-accusations continued between the two families.

articles.title: Bride Elopes a Day Before Wedding, Claims Forced Marriage; Kidnapping Case Takes Dramatic Turn
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Chitrakoot (Uttar Pradesh): A day before her scheduled wedding, a 25-year-old woman allegedly eloped with her lover from a beauty parlour in the Karvi police station area, triggering tension in the family and a kidnapping case.

body.html:
Chitrakoot (Uttar Pradesh): A day before her scheduled wedding, a 25-year-old woman allegedly eloped with her lover from a beauty parlour in the Karvi police station area, triggering tension in the family and a kidnapping case.

The incident took place in Chhapra Mafi village under the Kotwali area. Divya Shukla (25) was set to marry Dhananjay, a resident of Nagar village in Manikpur, with the wedding procession scheduled to arrive on February 12. Preparations were underway, and rituals were to begin on February 10.

On February 9, Divya’s father took her and her younger sister to Apoorva Beauty Parlour in Sitapur town for wedding makeup. After finishing her makeup, Divya allegedly stepped out while her sister remained inside. At that moment, she reportedly left in a car with her lover, Aditya Singh Chauhan. Despite her father’s attempt to stop her, she managed to flee.

Following the incident, her father lodged a complaint at Karvi police station, registering a kidnapping case against Aditya Singh Chauhan and two others — Shivendra and Garima Dixit.

However, the case took a new turn after Divya released a video on social media while sitting in a car with Aditya. In the video, she stated that she is 25 years old and had left home of her own free will. She alleged that her family was forcing her to marry an older man against her wishes and claimed she was subjected to mental and physical harassment.

Divya further claimed that she married Aditya Singh Chauhan in Prayagraj as per Arya Samaj rituals. Photographs and an alleged Arya Samaj marriage certificate have since gone viral on social media.

Police said efforts are underway to trace the woman and record her statement before a court. Officials added that if she is found to be a consenting adult and confirms her voluntary marriage, the kidnapping case may be legally impacted.

The incident has become a major talking point in the area, especially as the wedding was just a day away when the bride left with her lover.

#Chitrakoot #UttarPradesh #Karvi #BrideElopes #ForcedMarriage #AryaSamaj #ViralVideo #UPPolice #BreakingNews

articles.title: Party Turns Deadly: Woman Killed to ‘Eliminate Witness’ in Haldwani Double Murder
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Haldwani (Uttarakhand): A gruesome double murder has shocked the town after the bodies of a 19-year-old college student and a 25-year-old man were found with their heads crushed inside a godown at the Galla Mandi complex in the Naveen Mandi area on Bareilly Road on Thursday morning.

body.html:
Haldwani (Uttarakhand): A gruesome double murder has shocked the town after the bodies of a 19-year-old college student and a 25-year-old man were found with their heads crushed inside a godown at the Galla Mandi complex in the Naveen Mandi area on Bareilly Road on Thursday morning.

The deceased have been identified as Lakshmi Pokhariya (19), a BSc second-year student from Khansyu under Mukteshwar police station who was living in rented accommodation in Haldwani, and Shubham Tamta (25), a resident of Almora who worked as a supervisor at a rehabilitation centre in Haldwani.

According to police, both victims were allegedly attacked with large stones, and repeated blows to the head left their faces severely disfigured, making initial identification difficult. The bodies were discovered by labourers and traders when they arrived for work at the mandi.

Preliminary investigation revealed that the victims had attended a party on Wednesday night. Senior officers, including Manjunath TC, reached the spot to supervise the probe. A forensic team was deployed, CCTV footage from cameras installed in and around the mandi premises is being examined, and a dog squad was pressed into service. The crime scene was sealed and evidence collected.

An FIR was registered at Kotwali Haldwani under Section 103(1) of the BNS based on a complaint filed by the woman’s relative, Suresh Chandra Pokharia.

On February 13, police arrested four accused — Gaurav Negi (also known as Akku Thakur), Saurabh Bhatt, Deepu Sharma and Deepesh Latwal, all residents of Haldwani.

According to the SSP, the accused were drinking together when an argument broke out over the alleged harassment of the young woman. During the dispute, the group allegedly killed Shubham Tamta and later murdered Lakshmi Pokhariya to eliminate her as a witness.

The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. Further investigation is underway.

#Haldwani #Uttarakhand #DoubleMurder #CrimeNews #NaveenMandi #GallaMandi #BareillyRoad #BreakingNews #IndiaCrime

articles.title: Bathinda Police Solve Suitcase Murder Case; Victim’s Boyfriend Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bathinda (Punjab): The Bathinda Police have solved the murder of a 20-year-old woman whose partially burnt body was found stuffed in a suitcase near Behman Diwana village along the Bathinda–Malout highway on February 11.

body.html:
Bathinda (Punjab): The Bathinda Police have solved the murder of a 20-year-old woman whose partially burnt body was found stuffed in a suitcase near Behman Diwana village along the Bathinda–Malout highway on February 11.

The accused, 35-year-old Prince Kumar of Gulabgarh village, residing in the Surkhpeer area, has been arrested. Police have recovered the knife allegedly used in the murder and the car used to transport the body.

The victim has been identified as Sapna alias Mallika, a resident of Bagha Purana in Moga district, who was living in Bathinda. Police said she was married, though it is unclear whether her family was aware of her circumstances. Sources said her husband is currently in jail in a drug-related case.

Senior Superintendent of Police Jyoti Yadav said the accused confessed to killing Sapna at his residence on the morning of February 9. He allegedly stabbed her to death and attempted to burn the body inside a suitcase to destroy evidence. Fearing detection, he kept the body at home for two days before placing it in a new suitcase and dumping it near Behman Diwana on the intervening night of February 10–11.

Police recovered a fully burnt suitcase believed to have been used in the initial attempt to destroy evidence, and another new suitcase allegedly used to dispose of the body.

The victim was identified through her face and a tattoo. Call data records and CCTV footage revealed she was last seen with Prince Kumar on February 7. Around 15 suspects were examined before the accused was traced.

Police suspect a personal motive and described it as a crime of passion. The accused is reportedly a drug addict with no prior criminal record. The viscera report is awaited to determine if the victim had consumed drugs.

Further interrogation is underway.

#Bathinda #PunjabCrime #SuitcaseMurder #CrimeNews #BreakingNews #WomenSafety #PunjabPolice

articles.title: Hotel Worker Arrested in Aligarh After Viral Video Allegedly Shows Spitting on Rotis
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh): Tension prevailed in parts of Aligarh after a video surfaced on social media allegedly showing a hotel worker spitting on rotis while preparing them at a roadside eatery in the Gabhana area.

body.html:
Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh): Tension prevailed in parts of Aligarh after a video surfaced on social media allegedly showing a hotel worker spitting on rotis while preparing them at a roadside eatery in the Gabhana area.

The incident reportedly took place on February 12, 2026, at Rajput Hotel in Kalua village under the jurisdiction of Gabhana Police Station. The video quickly went viral, triggering anger among local residents and raising concerns over public health and communal harmony.

Police Action

According to an official press note issued on February 13, 2026, an FIR (No. 42/26) was registered under Sections 271 and 272 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 4 of the Epidemic Diseases Act.

Acting on the complaint, the Gabhana police team detained the accused, identified as Nasir Khan, son of Samand Khan, a resident of Kot Khas under Jawan police station in Aligarh district. He was taken into custody from Rajput Hotel in the Gabhana police station area. Further legal proceedings have been initiated.

Investigation Underway

Police stated that they took prompt cognizance of the viral video and registered a case to ensure public order and prevent the spread of misinformation. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the matter.

The police team involved in the action included Station House Officer Sachin Kumar, Sub-Inspector Harish Kumar, and Head Constable Satish Kumar of Gabhana police station.

Officials have urged citizens not to circulate unverified content and to maintain peace while the legal process is underway.

articles.title: High-Speed Crash on Lucknow–Kanpur Highway; Class 12 Student Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A six-year-old child lost his life and several others were injured in a tragic road accident on the Lucknow–Kanpur Highway on Thursday evening after a speeding car allegedly driven by a Class 12 student ran over pedestrians and rammed multiple vehicles.

body.html:
Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A six-year-old child lost his life and several others were injured in a tragic road accident on the Lucknow–Kanpur Highway on Thursday evening after a speeding car allegedly driven by a Class 12 student ran over pedestrians and rammed multiple vehicles.

The incident occurred around 7 pm near Hanuman Temple under the jurisdiction of Banthra Police Station, causing panic in the area.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Nipun Agarwal confirmed that four people sustained injuries, while six-year-old Dikshant Patel succumbed to his injuries during treatment. The accused, a resident of Bakshi Ka Talab in Lucknow, has been arrested and the vehicle involved in the accident has been seized.

Sequence of Events

According to preliminary findings, the student was returning from a farewell party and was accompanied by a girl at the time of the incident. Approximately 35 kilometres from Lucknow city, the speeding vehicle first collided with a tempo. It then went out of control, hitting pedestrians standing by the roadside before attempting to flee.

CCTV footage that has surfaced shows the car striking a motorcycle before ploughing into pedestrians and crashing into a tempo and an auto-rickshaw. The impact severely damaged the front portion of the car and led to chaos as locals rushed to assist the injured.

Victims

Among those injured were members of a family from Unnao — Sadhana Patel (35), her mother Meena Devi (60), and her son Dikshant (6). Dikshant was initially taken to a private hospital and later referred to the Sarojini Nagar Community Health Centre, where he died during treatment.

Others injured include e-rickshaw driver Awadh Bihari (42) and a 12-year-old boy who had come to the market for shopping. All injured persons are undergoing treatment.

Attempt to Escape and Arrest

Eyewitnesses stated that locals attempted to apprehend the driver, but he accelerated in an effort to escape, causing further injuries. The girl accompanying him was stopped by the crowd and handed over to the police. Based on her statement, authorities tracked down the vehicle and arrested the accused driver.

Police have registered a case and launched a detailed investigation. CCTV footage and eyewitness testimonies are being examined to establish the precise sequence of events and determine accountability.

Further legal action will follow based on the outcome of the investigation.

articles.title: Mid-Day Meal Milk Dilution Alleged at Mahoba Primary School; Inquiry Ordered
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mahoba (Uttar Pradesh): A disturbing allegation regarding the mid-day meal scheme has surfaced from Dhikwaha village in Mahoba district, raising serious concerns about the functioning of the local education administration.

body.html:
Mahoba (Uttar Pradesh): A disturbing allegation regarding the mid-day meal scheme has surfaced from Dhikwaha village in Mahoba district, raising serious concerns about the functioning of the local education administration.

A viral video circulating on social media purportedly shows milk being heavily diluted before distribution to students at a government primary school in the village. In the footage, a cook identified as Chhabirani is seen pouring only two packets of milk into a bucket filled with water. The mixture turns lightly white and is then allegedly served to children.

The video also appears to show the act taking place in the presence of the school’s principal, Monica Soni. In a separate clip, the principal is allegedly seen sleeping in the classroom while students are present.

According to villagers, the incident reflects not just negligence but potential misuse of funds allocated under the government’s mid-day meal scheme. Locals have alleged irregularities in both food quality and academic supervision at the school, claiming that standards are being compromised at the expense of children’s health and education.

The mid-day meal programme is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at improving nutritional levels among school-going children and encouraging enrolment and attendance in government schools.

Taking cognizance of the viral videos, Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Rahul Mishra has ordered an inquiry into the matter. He stated that strict action will be taken if the allegations are found to be true following verification of the footage.

Authorities have yet to officially confirm the authenticity of the videos. The investigation is currently underway.

articles.title: Etah Police Refute Viral Claims of Caste-Based Attack on Dalit Wedding Procession
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Etah (Uttar Pradesh): The Etah Police has issued a detailed clarification regarding a viral video alleging a caste-based attack on a Jatav wedding procession in the district, calling the claims misleading and potentially inflammatory.

body.html:
Etah (Uttar Pradesh): The Etah Police has issued a detailed clarification regarding a viral video alleging a caste-based attack on a Jatav wedding procession in the district, calling the claims misleading and potentially inflammatory.

The controversy began after a video circulated widely on social media platform X, in which a woman from the Jatav community alleged that members of the Shakya community stopped their wedding baraat, hurled casteist slurs, and assaulted participants. The video triggered concerns about rising caste tensions in the region.

However, police officials have presented a different version of events. According to authorities, the incident occurred under the jurisdiction of the Sakit Police Station on the night between February 10 and 11.

Police Version of Events

Police stated that the Jatav wedding procession proceeded without obstruction. During the return journey, members of the procession allegedly entered a Shakya family’s engagement ceremony, where music was being played and guests were celebrating.

According to the police investigation, some individuals from the Jatav group reportedly entered the venue uninvited, demanded that the DJ music be stopped, and engaged in abusive behaviour. This allegedly led to a clash between the two sides, resulting in injuries to two Shakya youths.

The Shakya family subsequently filed a complaint.

Authorities further identified the woman seen in the viral video as the wife of one of the accused from the Jatav side. Police stated that the video was recorded after the incident and allegedly intended to shift blame onto the Shakya community.

Official Statement

Additional Superintendent of Police Shwetabh Pandey released a video statement on X, clarifying that the Jatav wedding procession was not attacked. He termed the viral claims “misleading and incorrect,” adding that legal action is being taken based on the complaint received.

Police also indicated that there were attempts to frame the matter under provisions of the SC/ST Act against the Shakya community, but said their investigation prevented any misuse of the law.

Social Context

In Uttar Pradesh, the Jatav community is classified under the Scheduled Caste category, while the Shakya community falls under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category.

The incident has underscored the sensitivity of caste-related allegations and the role of social media in amplifying unverified narratives. Police have urged citizens to refrain from spreading unverified claims and to rely on official statements.

Further investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Elderly Woman Allegedly Assaulted at Old Age Home in Lucknow; Police Begin Probe
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A disturbing video allegedly showing an elderly woman being physically assaulted at an old age home in the Rajajipuram area of Lucknow has triggered widespread outrage.

body.html:
Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh): A disturbing video allegedly showing an elderly woman being physically assaulted at an old age home in the Rajajipuram area of Lucknow has triggered widespread outrage.

The incident is reported from Krishna Dharmarth Ashram, located at B-86 near Jalalpur Phatak in Rajajipuram. The facility, which functions as an NGO-run old age home and reportedly receives government funding, is now facing serious allegations of inhuman treatment and physical abuse of residents.

According to viral video footage circulating on social media, the ashram’s manager is seen allegedly slapping an elderly woman. The visuals have sparked anger among citizens, with many questioning the safety and dignity of senior citizens housed in such institutions.

The ashram, which is meant to serve as a place of support, care and security for the elderly, is now under scrutiny. Allegations suggest that despite receiving lakhs of rupees annually in government assistance in the name of charitable service, residents may be subjected to mistreatment.

Responding to the controversy, the Talkatora Police Station confirmed that it has taken cognizance of the viral video. Police officials stated that an investigation is currently underway and that appropriate legal action will be taken based on the findings.

Authorities have not yet released details regarding the authenticity of the video, the condition of the elderly woman, or whether any formal complaint has been filed.

The incident has reignited debate over monitoring mechanisms, accountability of NGO-run care homes, and the enforcement of senior citizen protection laws in Uttar Pradesh.

Further updates are awaited as the investigation progresses.
